title: A Message to Baruch

questions.question: To whom did Jeremiah the prophet speak the word recorded in this chapter, in the fourth year of Jehoiakim?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 45:1 (ESV): "The word that Jeremiah the prophet spoke to Baruch the son of Neriah, when he wrote these words in a book at the dictation of Jeremiah, in the fourth year of Jehoiakim..."

questions.question: What had Baruch said that the Lord overheard and addressed?
options: "Woe is me! For the Lord has added sorrow to my pain; I am weary with my groaning, and I find no rest."
"Why has God forsaken us? Let us flee to Babylon!"
"The king is evil, he must be destroyed."
"I refuse to write these words of disaster."
questions.correctAnswer: "Woe is me! For the Lord has added sorrow to my pain; I am weary with my groaning, and I find no rest."
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 45:3 (ESV): "You said, 'Woe is me! For the Lord has added sorrow to my pain; I am weary with my groaning, and I find no rest.'"

questions.question: The Lord told Baruch: "Behold, what I have built I am breaking down, and what I have planted I am plucking up—that is, the whole..."
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 45:4 (ESV): "Behold, what I have built I am breaking down, and what I have planted I am plucking up—that is, the whole land."

questions.question: What did the Lord instruct Baruch NOT to seek for himself?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 45:5 (ESV): "And do you seek great things for yourself? Seek them not,"

questions.question: "...for behold, I am bringing disaster upon all flesh, declares the Lord. But I will give you your... as a prize of war in all places to which you may go."
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 45:5 (ESV): "But I will give you your life as a prize of war in all places to which you may go."

questions.question: In what year of Jehoiakim the son of Josiah did Jeremiah speak this word to Baruch?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 45:1 (ESV): "in the fourth year of Jehoiakim the son of Josiah, king of Judah:"

questions.question: How did Baruch record these words?
options: He wrote them in a book at the dictation of Jeremiah
He memorized them to repeat to the king
He sent them by letter to the exiles
questions.correctAnswer: He wrote them in a book at the dictation of Jeremiah
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 45:1 (ESV): "when he wrote these words in a book at the dictation of Jeremiah,"

questions.question: Who is the ultimate source of the message to Baruch?
options: The Lord, the God of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: The Lord, the God of Israel
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 45:2 (ESV): "Thus says the Lord, the God of Israel, to you, O Baruch:"

questions.question: To what cause did Baruch attribute his sorrow and pain in verse 3?
options: The Lord had added sorrow to his pain
questions.correctAnswer: The Lord had added sorrow to his pain
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 45:3 (ESV): "You said, 'Woe is me! For the Lord has added sorrow to my pain...'"

questions.question: Baruch said he was weary with his groaning and found no what?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 45:3 (ESV): "I am weary with my groaning, and I find no rest."

questions.question: What is the implied emotional state of Baruch in this chapter?
questions.explanation: Baruch is "weary with groaning" and "finds no rest" because of the disaster about to fall on the nation.

questions.question: What phrase does God use to describe the widespread judgment coming?
options: "I am bringing disaster upon all flesh"
"I am throwing fire on the earth"
"A great storm is rising from the north"
"The sun will go dark at noon"
questions.correctAnswer: "I am bringing disaster upon all flesh"
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 45:5 (ESV): "for behold, I am bringing disaster upon all flesh, declares the Lord."

questions.question: The phrase "your life as a prize of war" also appears earlier in Jeremiah regarding what other individual?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah also gave this promise from God to Ebed-melech the Ethiopian in chapter 39. (also chapter 21 to those who surrender).

questions.question: What is the primary divine action described in Jeremiah 45:4?
options: Breaking down and plucking up what was built and planted
Establishing a new king in Jerusalem
questions.correctAnswer: Breaking down and plucking up what was built and planted
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 45:4 (ESV): "Behold, what I have built I am breaking down, and what I have planted I am plucking up..."

questions.question: Is chapter 45 placed chronologically in the book of Jeremiah?
options: No, it dates back to Jehoiakim's reign (before chapters 37-44)
Yes, it happened right after they arrived in Egypt
No, it refers to the time of Josiah
questions.correctAnswer: No, it dates back to Jehoiakim's reign (before chapters 37-44)
questions.explanation: Chapters 37-44 deal with Zedekiah's reign and the aftermath of the fall of Jerusalem. Chapter 45 flashes back to the "fourth year of Jehoiakim" (aligning with chapter 36).

key_verse_text: "And do you seek great things for yourself? Seek them not, for behold, I am bringing disaster upon all flesh, declares the Lord. But I will give you your life as a prize of war in all places to which you may go."
